skill.name: scaffolding-fastapi-dapr
skill.description: Scaffold FastAPI services with SQLModel persistence, Dapr pub/sub and jobs, JWT authentication, testing, logging, and layered application patterns.
skill.summary: Build structured FastAPI and Dapr backends with database, authentication, messaging, and testing guidance.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are lexical false positives involving SQLModel query methods, Markdown formatting, local URLs, and documented configuration. Confirmed risks include an unpinned remote installer piped to bash and SQL query logging, while semantic review found weak JWT validation, unauthenticated Dapr handlers, forced message acknowledgement, and error leakage.

remediation.issue: The Dapr installation command executes an unpinned remote script.
remediation.suggestion: Download a version-pinned release, verify its checksum or signature, inspect it, and execute it as a separate step.

remediation.issue: JWT examples omit issuer validation and disable or omit audience validation.
remediation.suggestion: Require expected issuer and audience claims, validate expiration, select the matching key, and reject tokens with missing required claims.

remediation.issue: Dapr callback examples accept and persist unauthenticated event data.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict callback routes to the sidecar, require Dapr API tokens or mTLS, validate schemas, and enforce idempotency.

remediation.issue: Database examples enable SQLAlchemy echo logging.
remediation.suggestion: Disable echo logging outside local development and configure structured logging to redact credentials, tokens, and sensitive parameters.

remediation.issue: Dapr handlers return success after processing exceptions.
remediation.suggestion: Return retryable failures for transient errors and use a dead-letter topic for permanently invalid messages.

remediation.issue: Authentication and database exceptions are returned directly to clients.
remediation.suggestion: Return stable generic error messages and retain detailed exception data only in access-controlled server logs.

semantic_findings.title: Incomplete JWT Claim Validation
semantic_findings.description: The authentication guidance omits issuer validation and disables or omits audience validation, allowing valid tokens intended for another service to be accepted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: One example performs signature decoding without issuer or audience constraints, and the detailed example explicitly disables audience verification.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated Dapr Event Handlers
semantic_findings.description: The examples accept event payloads and write derived records without authenticating the sidecar or authorizing the message source.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both handler examples process request bodies without an authentication dependency, signature check, API token, or documented network restriction.

semantic_findings.title: Errors Are Acknowledged as Successful
semantic_findings.description: The Dapr guidance returns success after processing exceptions, which suppresses retries and can cause permanent event loss.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guidance explicitly instructs handlers to return SUCCESS even when processing raises an exception.

semantic_findings.title: Internal Exceptions Returned to Clients
semantic_findings.description: Authentication and database examples include raw exception text in HTTP responses, which can expose implementation details and operational data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both examples interpolate caught exception strings directly into client-visible HTTP error details.

content.value_statement: Building consistent FastAPI microservices requires coordinated database, authentication, messaging, and testing patterns. This skill supplies reusable guidance for SQLModel, Dapr, JWT, logging, and service architecture.
actual_capabilities: Defines SQLModel database, request, response, and update schemas.
Shows synchronous and asynchronous FastAPI CRUD endpoint patterns.
Provides Dapr pub/sub, CloudEvent, state, and scheduled job guidance.
Covers JWT and JWKS authentication with FastAPI dependencies.
Includes repository, service, logging, testing, migration, and versioning patterns.
limitations: Provides patterns and scaffolding guidance, not a complete deployable repository.
Requires project-specific authorization, tenant isolation, and data validation decisions.
Dapr examples assume a configured sidecar, components, and supporting infrastructure.
Security-sensitive examples require the remediations identified in this audit.

use_cases.title: Create a Service Foundation
use_cases.description: Generate a consistent FastAPI structure with SQLModel schemas, database sessions, CRUD routes, and tests.
use_cases.target_user: Backend developers starting a new Python service

use_cases.title: Add Event-Driven Workflows
use_cases.description: Introduce Dapr subscriptions, event publishing, CloudEvent handling, and scheduled callbacks.

use_cases.title: Standardize Backend Patterns
use_cases.description: Apply repository, service, authentication, logging, versioning, and test conventions across multiple APIs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter API
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a FastAPI service for [domain]. Include SQLModel create, update, table, and response models with basic CRUD routes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new backend

prompt_templates.title: Add Persistence and Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend my FastAPI service with asynchronous PostgreSQL sessions and JWT authentication. Validate issuer, audience, expiration, and the matching JWKS key.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Dapr Messaging
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Dapr pub/sub to this service for [topic]. Include authenticated handlers, CloudEvent validation, idempotency, retries, and dead-letter handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this FastAPI backend into repository and service layers. Add structured logging, migrations, versioned routes, integration tests, and deployment checks.

output_examples.input: Create a task API with PostgreSQL persistence.
output: A layered project structure for routes, models, database sessions, repositories, and services.
Separate create, update, table, and response models with validated fields.
CRUD behavior with transaction ownership, pagination, error handling, and focused tests.

output_examples.input: Add Dapr events when tasks are created.
output: A publishing flow through the local Dapr sidecar.
A validated subscription handler that unwraps CloudEvents and enforces idempotency.
Retry and dead-letter behavior that preserves failed messages.

output_examples.input: Protect routes with an external JWKS provider.
output: A cached JWKS retrieval design with matching key selection.
JWT checks for algorithm, issuer, audience, expiration, and required claims.
A FastAPI authentication dependency with generic client errors.

best_practices: Keep API schemas separate from database table models.
Let route or service boundaries own transactions and refresh objects after commits.
Validate authentication claims, event sources, payload schemas, and retry behavior before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not execute remote installation scripts without pinning and integrity verification.
Do not expose Dapr callback routes without authentication or network restrictions.
Do not return raw exceptions or enable SQL query logging in production.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete application?
faq.answer: It provides implementation patterns and scaffolding guidance. You must integrate generated pieces with your project configuration and domain rules.

faq.question: Which database patterns are covered?
faq.answer: It covers SQLModel with PostgreSQL or SQLite, synchronous and asynchronous sessions, relationships, queries, migrations, and test databases.

faq.question: Which Dapr features are included?
faq.answer: It covers pub/sub subscriptions, CloudEvent handling, publishing, state patterns, sidecar configuration, and scheduled jobs.

faq.question: Does it support JWT authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance uses JWKS-based verification, but production implementations must validate issuer, audience, expiration, and required claims.

faq.question: Can I use it without Dapr?
faq.answer: Yes. FastAPI, SQLModel, testing, logging, repository, and service patterns can be applied independently.

faq.question: What should I review before deployment?
faq.answer: Review authorization, secret handling, Dapr endpoint protection, JWT claims, database logging, error responses, migrations, and integration tests.
